title: Investigating Composite Modeling in Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization for Scientific Design
abstract: arXiv:2611.13565v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Scientific design often requires balancing competing objectives that are expensive to evaluate through experiments or simulations. Multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) addresses this challenge by using probabilistic models to guide the selection of promising designs. In many applications, tunable inputs map to observable intermediate responses, which are then combined through known functions to compute the final objectives. Prior work on Bayesian optimization of composite functions shows that learning from these intermediate responses, which we call Composite modeling, can substantially improve sampling efficiency in single-objective optimization, compared to methods that condition only on black-box observations of the objective function. translated_title: 面向科学设计的多目标贝叶斯优化中复合建模的研究
translated_abstract: 科学设计通常需要在相互冲突的目标之间进行权衡，而这些目标通过实验或仿真进行评估的代价十分高昂。多目标贝叶斯优化（MOBO）通过使用概率模型来指导有前景设计的选择，从而应对这一挑战。在许多应用中，可调输入会映射到可观测的中间响应，随后通过已知函数将这些中间响应组合起来以计算最终目标。先前关于复合函数贝叶斯优化的研究表明，从这些中间响应中学习（我们称之为复合建模），与仅依赖目标函数黑盒观测的方法相比，能够显著提高单目标优化中的采样效率。然而，复合建模在MOBO中的收益仍缺乏充分研究。在本工作中，我们研究了复合建模在MOBO中的收益，并探究了导致其表现变化的因素。
tldr: 本文系统研究了利用可观测中间响应的复合建模在多目标贝叶斯优化中对科学设计的收益，并探究了影响其效果差异的因素。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically investigates the benefits of composite modeling—leveraging observable intermediate responses—in multi-objective Bayesian optimization for scientific design, and examines the factors driving its performance variation.
